newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ electoral officer says high vote indicated.
newsitem.headline: NZ electoral officer says high vote indicated.

text.p: New Zealand Chief Electoral Officer Phil Whelan said on Friday that heavy special voting indicated a high turnout in Saturday's general election.
Whelan told TV1 that he was surprised by the high number of special votes cast already.
"It would appear, in judging that back against 1993, that probably it's about three times the volume that we had in 1993.
"That suggests that maybe on polling day we may be up to around 90 percent of voter turnout and for the 1993 election we had 85 percent," he said.

Whelan said last election there were 190,000 special votes cast by people abroad or outside their home electorate on polling day. Special votes cannot by law be finally tallied until 10 days after election day.
Whelan said the electoral office expects to have the majority of votes in by 11.00 p.m. (1000 GMT) on election night.
Voting opens at 9.00 a.m. (2000 GMT on Friday) and ends at 7.00 p.m. (0600 GMT).
